prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Create one extraordinary wide landscape editorial cover for The ARC Daily Digest's commissioned special afternoon feature about Kenneth Stanley and the difficulty of benchmarking open-ended discovery. Primary visual: an impossible self-growing ecosystem constructed entirely from crisp ARC puzzle grids, colored square tiles and black gridlines. In the foreground a simple flat black square grid with a few red, blue, yellow and green cells physically unfolds upward into a surreal branching world: tiled staircases become bridges, a bridge sprouts a different grid with a new pattern, that grid grows an archipelago of geometrical creatures and little architectural laboratories, and their tiny inventions become the stepping stones for further worlds. Show several genuinely different branches of invention, some modest detours, one surprising loop or portal where a grid creates another grid that starts creating an entirely different world. A tiny anonymous mechanical explorer follows one unexpected side path. The central metaphor is cumulative discovery, not just identical infinitely nested squares. Make it wonderfully weird but legible, a sophisticated science-magazine illustration, intricate tactile paper sculpture blended with painterly isometric engraving. Rich midnight navy space, ivory paper grid faces, vivid ARC red blue yellow green magenta cyan orange accents, warm light emerging from inventions. A beautiful asymmetric sweeping upward composition with clear foreground-to-background depth and a sense that the frame cannot contain the next invention. No real people, no likenesses, no company logos, no invented data, no scores, no arrows masquerading as a measured chart. This is conceptual art, not an announced ARC-4 task. Finish as a polished newspaper cover with an integrated quiet dark strip across the bottom containing exact typography: small masthead 'THE ARC DAILY DIGEST'; large ivory headline 'THE OPEN-ENDEDNESS OF OPEN-ENDEDNESS'; small line 'KENNETH STANLEY AND THE BENCHMARK AFTER GAMES'; compact edition/date 'SPECIAL AFTERNOON EDITION · 29 OCTOBER 2026'; tiny credit 'AI editorial illustration'. Keep text away from the main visual, perfectly spelled, elegant and readable. Landscape aspect ratio about 3:2. Opaque background.
